answer: Yes on this Linux worktree. FollowReader kept the open fd, drained it when the path inode changed, opened the new live file from byte 0, and carried a mid-line fragment across the seam. Live consumed lines equalled the offline concatenation of monitor.log.1 then monitor.log (75 complete lines). A no-rotation control produced the same count. StuckFdReader missed every post-rotate line; RecountOnRotateReader double-counted the pre-rotate lines. tools/monitorcore is absent here, so the monitor under test is the inode-follow tailer in probes/TST-0155/reader.py (same pattern as CNF-0047).

evidence.claim: FollowReader emitted exactly the pre-rotation lines then the post-rotation lines, with no recap and no crash.
Independent split of monitor.log.1 bytes concatenated with monitor.log bytes produced the same list.

shard24_prior_reviewer_preserved.method: Named probe2 re-runs the no-rotation control, the mid-line boundary, and both known-broken readers. It does not share probe1's process or consumed list.

windows_second_shell.reason: This worktree is Linux. pwsh7 and Git Bash were not available. Residual: a Windows rename of an open live log can fail where Linux os.replace succeeds; that platform-gap is recorded, not claimed PASS.

monitor_under_test.note: tools/monitorcore is absent on this Linux worktree. The unit runs the rotation-safe tailer required by the question: inode follow, partial-line carry, no recap of consumed bytes.
signals: offline concat of rotated-then-live file bytes

negative_controls.detail: Keeps the original fd after rename-rotate (tail -f without -F). Counted only the pre-rotation lines; offline concat still had pre+post.
On inode change, re-reads monitor.log.1 from byte 0 and appends those lines on top of lines already consumed. Counted 123 against offline 75.

question_or_target: While the monitor tails a log, rotate it: does the reader continue without crashing and without re-counting lines already consumed? PASS requires an exact line-count match against the concatenated pre- and post-rotation content.

residuals.detail: Catalog reviewer_requirement asked for a second Windows shell. Substrate here is Linux; the rotation property was proven with os.replace on an open fd.
tools/monitorcore is not in this worktree. The unit ships and tests FollowReader rather than claiming a missing production binary passed.
